answer: In PoA, identity verification binds each identity to a Wesolowski VDF whose evaluation requires continuous sequential modular squarings. A single chain cannot be divided across GPUs to reduce its inherent depth. An attacker creating clones must execute a separate time-lock computation for every identity; hardware can run chains concurrently, but cannot eliminate each chain’s sequential delay. Consequently, velvet, vertex, and vault identities carry a strict physical cost, providing sybil resistance.
